public_rationale: The poll reports local data-center opposition among 69% of Democrats, 54% of Republicans and 53% of independents. Those results clearly support substantial opposition across party lines, even though its strength differs by party.
limitations: The claim concerns public sentiment, not agreement among elected officials.
Subgroup estimates have sampling uncertainty; the claim does not require proving that each population share exceeds 50%.
The question concerns new local construction.

from_speaker: it is a sentiment that crosses party lines

our_interpretation: The sentiment is opposition to constructing new data centers in respondents' own areas.
Crosses party lines ordinarily means substantial opposition among both Democrats and Republicans. It does not require equal opposition, unanimity or agreement among party leaders.
The target period is June 16–July 19, 2026, the fieldwork period of the new poll referenced in the post.
criteria.support_condition: The poll's party breakdown shows substantial local data-center opposition among both Democrats and Republicans; opposition among independents provides additional support.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The party breakdown shows opposition concentrated in one major party and only marginal opposition in the other.
